title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-25
content:
Quick log / scratchpad for GPU ops and infra TODOs (working notes)

2026-03-03 -> 2026-03-04 notes:
- Morning: triaged NVLink flaps on g4-pool-3 (node g4-03). Root cause looks like driver/kernel mismatch after security patch.
  - Action: rollback driver to 525.89.02 on g4-03, monitor for 2h.
  - Ticket: JIRA-OPS-412 (linked) assigned to @Maya.
- Capacity request for Q2 burst: finance asked for rough numbers. Need to update capacity plan spreadsheet with: expected peak tokens/day, avg concurrency, target p99 latency (200ms).
  - TODO: pull last 7d qps from /metrics/rr-agg and update sheet (deadline 2026-03-06).
- Autoscaler: observed slow scale-up on dedicated pools when cold starts hit. Hypothesis: VM spin-up + scheduler throttling.
  - Experiment idea: pre-warm policy for canary route (5% traffic) -> keep 1 warm instance per AZ.
  - Action: propose config change in infra repo (PR template in linked PR 987) and run load test.
- Networking: noticed intermittent packet drops between region-a and region-b (10:45-11:15 UTC). Probable MTU mismatch on transit device.
  - Quick check: run ping/path MTU + traceroute on affected nodes (g4-01..g4-05).
- Runbook updates needed:
  - GPU node driver rollback steps (add note about kernel-version pinning).
  - NVLink alert playbook: add automated rollback + slack notify to #gpu-ops.

Short TODOs (priority order):
1) Patch rollbacks: finish rollback on g4-03 and confirm stable (Ethan + Maya).
2) Update capacity spreadsheet with 7d metrics, add Q2 burst estimate (Ethan) - due 2026-03-06.
3) Draft autoscaler pre-warm PR (branch: autoscaler/prewarm) and run bench (Luis to help).
4) Run MTU checks and open ticket with network team if confirmed (Ethan).
5) Add NVLink rollback steps to confluence runbook (Maya) - include exact driver versions and kernel pins.

Notes to self / commands:
- driver rollback command (tested):
  sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-525=525.89.02-0ubuntu1 && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-device-plugin
- check node logs: journalctl -u nvidia-device-plugin -n 500 --no-pager
- quick metrics: curl -s "https://metrics.internal/rr-agg?start=168&end=0&metric=gpu_util" | jq '.summary'

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we standardize on a single driver version per quarter and block security autopatches that change kernel ABI? (risk vs security)
- Can we add an automated canary for driver upgrades that runs perf smoke tests before fleet-wide rollout?

Slack refs / links:
- #gpu-ops - post rollback status and tag @oncall
- #infra - for autoscaler config PR review

Misc notes (brain dump):
- Billing: add note to check committed-use discounts if Q2 burst becomes persistent.
- Consider snapshotting g4-03 before big changes (safe point).

End of scratchpad entry.
